codeReview.summary: Solid implementation of 8 new queue/step lifecycle event types. All events correctly added to FlywheelEvent union, FlywheelEmitter interface and implementation, and all 3 adapters (opentui, headless, mock). The worker correctly identified a naming collision with existing StepStarted/StepCompleted/StepFailed types (which use step:started/step:completed/step:failed discriminants with phaseIndex/stepIndex payloads) and chose QueueStepStarted/queue:step-started etc. to avoid breaking the discriminated union — a necessary and well-reasoned deviation from the feature description's literal naming. Exhaustiveness checks pass. Existing events preserved. Tests cover all 8 new types plus 3 existing event preservation checks (12 tests total). Two non-blocking issues found.

issues.description: stepType field uses 'string' instead of StepType from src/queue/types.ts. This applies to all 5 queue step event interfaces (QueueStepStarted, QueueStepCompleted, QueueStepFailed, QueueStepInserted, QueueStepRemoved). Using the StepType union ('plan' | 'work' | 'review' | 'ship' | 'debug' | 'research' | 'verify' | 'gate') would provide compile-time safety and prevent callers from passing arbitrary strings. The corresponding emitter method signatures in event-bus.ts would also need updating.

queue:step-failed handler omits stepTitle from log metadata ({workflowId, stepId, stepType, reason}) while queue:step-started and queue:step-completed both include it ({workflowId, stepId, stepType, stepTitle}). stepTitle is arguably more useful in failure logs for debugging. Should be consistent across all three handlers.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The worker chose QueueStepStarted/queue:step-started naming instead of the feature description's StepStarted/step:started to avoid discriminated union collision with existing types. This naming convention (prefixing with Queue* and queue:* namespace for queue-related events) should be documented so future features follow the same pattern consistently rather than re-discovering the collision.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: src/events/types.ts lines 113-130 define existing StepStarted/StepCompleted/StepFailed with step:started/step:completed/step:failed discriminants and phaseIndex/stepIndex payloads. New QueueStepStarted etc. at lines 445-493 use queue:step-started etc. Worker transcript shows detailed analysis of the collision before choosing the naming.

sharedStateObservations.observation: Event interfaces use 'string' for stepType field instead of the StepType union from src/queue/types.ts. The events module (src/events/) doesn't import from src/queue/types.ts. There's no documented convention about whether event interfaces should use domain-specific types or keep loose typing for forward compatibility. This should be decided and documented.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: src/events/types.ts lines 449, 458, 467, 479, 490 all use 'stepType: string' while src/queue/types.ts lines 26-35 defines StepType as a strict union.

summary: PASS. Clean implementation of 8 queue/step lifecycle event types with correct union integration, emitter methods, and exhaustive adapter handling. The worker made a sound judgment call renaming step events to queue:step-* namespace to avoid colliding with existing step:* events. Two non-blocking issues: stepType should use StepType union instead of string for type safety, and queue:step-failed log in OpenTUI adapter is missing stepTitle. All tests pass (4312 total, 12 new), typecheck clean.
